sections.overview: The floral banded wobbegong is a small carpet shark known from the continental shelf off southwestern Australia.
sections.identification: Its yellowish-brown pattern combines bands, blotches, spots and reticulated markings; this combination helps distinguish it from other wobbegongs.
sections.habitat: It occurs between Geraldton and Augusta in Western Australia, at recorded depths of 42–85 m.
sections.diet: Its diet has not been studied in detail; prey patterns reported for other wobbegongs should not be treated as direct observations of this species.
sections.behavior: Few direct observations are available, so its activity pattern and hunting behavior remain poorly documented.
sections.reproduction: Reproduction is presumed viviparous, but species-specific details have not been established.
sections.ecology: Described alongside O. parvimaculatus in 2008, it is distinguished from that sympatric cousin by a combination of colour, morphology and measurements; see that profile for the reciprocal comparison.
sections.conservation: The 2025 global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern, while noting its naturally restricted range.
